name: Zany
why: Probably the cleanest performance-liveaboard overlap found so far: 3-cabin/3-head owner version, never chartered, upgraded twin 57hp Yanmars, 1,200Ah Relion lithium, ~1,680W total solar, Victron 5kW inverter, 9kW Onan, full ~40k-BTU A/C designed to run from batteries, 15 GPH watermaker, washer/dryer, radar/AIS/Iridium and extensive cruising gear. Owners reportedly want a quick sale and the boat has spent recent years in fresh water.
risks: ~3,000h engines and ~4,500h generator as of Sep. 2024. Standing-rig replacement date, saildrive service/diaphragm history, current battery capacity, recent survey/moisture/casualty history and exact A/C overnight endurance need documentation. Broker is explicitly pushing for a quick cash buyer, so diligence discipline matters.
stage: New performance lead — not contacted; outreach strongly recommended
next_step: Recommended outreach: request recent survey, rig/saildrive history, engine/genset service, lithium test data, actual overnight A/C battery use, damage/insurance history and realistic deal range after the fresh reduction. Do not discuss travel until records land.
listed_date_notes: Current MLS record showed Last Updated Dec 25, 2025; a withdrawn 2023 offering is not carried forward.
notes: HIGH-PRIORITY PERFORMANCE-LIVEABOARD LEAD. This is the closest current-market answer to 'faster Lagoon 450 without giving up the floating-home systems.'

name: Catana 42 – Guadeloupe
why: Genuine performance-cruiser in ideal Caribbean geography: carbon/Kevlar/GRP infusion construction, lifting daggerboards, only ~800h on Volvo D2-40s, recent lithium, substantial solar, watermaker, Raymarine/Garmin/AIS, recent hydraulic autopilot and recent furling genoa. Listing presents it as immediately ready for long-distance cruising.
risks: 4-cabin/2-head rather than owner-suite layout. Exact lithium/solar capacities, standing-rig replacement date, mainsail age, saildrive diaphragm/service history, generator/A-C status, survey/moisture/casualty history and structural repair history are not disclosed in the public listing.
refit_display: $15–40k pending A/C, rig and detailed systems diligence
stage: New performance lead — not contacted; outreach strongly recommended
next_step: Recommended outreach: get current survey, exact solar/lithium specification, rig/sail dates, saildrive service/diaphragms, A/C/generator status, damage/insurance history and seller flexibility. Ask whether a 4-cabin-to-owner-suite conversion is structurally/practically sensible on this hull.
listed_date_notes: Earliest dated MLS image in listing 10167769 is Apr 30, 2026.
notes: HIGH-PRIORITY PERFORMANCE-LIVEABOARD LEAD. At roughly the same acquisition cost as our strongest Lagoon/FP candidates, it materially changes the speed/comfort tradeoff.

name: Pippin
why: Rare combination of real performance and a nearly ideal off-grid refit: 3-cabin/2-head owner version, never chartered, carbon mast/daggerboards, 1,200Ah lithium and 3,080W solar from 2022, full Victron suite, DC A/C, Spectra watermaker, newer running rigging and major standing-rig components, radar/AIS/SSB, hardtop and extensive 2022 safety/anchoring work. Generator-free design is intentional.
risks: 2001 hull with original 56hp Yanmars at ~5,058/4,290h and older SD31 saildrives. Full standing-rig renewal is not one-date/simple: forestay/shrouds/headstay were replaced 2020–21 while diamond rods remain. Hull-deck joint was fully reefed/recaulked in 2022, which needs context and documentation. Sail ages are not clearly disclosed.
stage: New performance lead — not contacted; outreach strongly recommended
next_step: Recommended outreach: request recent survey/moisture report, hull-deck-joint work file, engine/saildrive service and oil analysis, remaining standing-rig/diamond history, sail ages, lithium installation documentation and realistic seller floor after the large price reduction.
listed_date_notes: Earliest dated MLS media is Aug 26, 2025; the broker page was republished Feb 2, 2026.
notes: HIGH-PRIORITY VALUE/PERFORMANCE LEAD. Age is the reason it is not an automatic #1, but the 2022 energy system is unusually aligned with Max's desired spec.

name: Plot Twist
why: 38-ft performance-oriented owner version that is unusually well refitted for immediate cruising: 900Ah ReLion lithium, 1,600W REC solar, Victron 3kW, 30 GPH Rainman watermaker, 18k-BTU Dometic A/C installed 2025, standing rigging 2024/25, Dyneema running rig 2026, 2025 radar/electronics and recent Autoprops. Proven Bahamas cruising and strong indoor/outdoor liveability.
risks: Twin original Yanmar 3GM30s show ~5,000h each. Only a portable Honda EU2200i generator; A/C is one 18k-BTU unit. At 38 ft it gives up storage, payload and owner's-suite volume versus 42–46 ft options. Engine/saildrive replacement horizon and current sail ages need diligence.
stage: New performance lead — not contacted; outreach recommended
next_step: Recommended outreach: request engine/saildrive service history and oil analysis, current survey, sail dates, lithium/solar invoices, A/C real-world overnight draw and casualty/moisture history. Main decision is whether 38 ft is enough full-time living space for Max.
listed_date_notes: Earliest dated MLS media is Mar 24, 2026; the broker page was published May 13.
notes: SERIOUS PERFORMANCE-LIVEABOARD VALUE. Systems are much closer to target than most sub-$350k boats; size and 5k-hour engines are the tradeoffs.

name: Delphine
why: True high-performance bluewater cat with daggerboards and documented race/passage pedigree. ~1,530h Yanmars, saildrives previously rebuilt including membranes, standing rigging replaced 2023, 300Ah Victron lithium fitted 2023, ~960W tilting solar, updated electronics/autopilot, washer, Coppercoat and years of professional incremental maintenance in Grenada.
risks: 2003 design gives up substantially more interior volume and payload than Lagoon/Nautitech. Only 300Ah lithium and 960W solar; no permanent A/C disclosed and watermaker capacity is unclear. Sail ages need exact dates despite low seasonal use. Verify structural/core history and details of the original major bottom/refit work.
refit_display: $25–60k comfort/electrical reserve depending A/C, watermaker and battery target
stage: New performance lead — not contacted; secondary outreach candidate
next_step: Worth outreach after Zany/Catana/Pippin: request current survey, exact watermaker/electrical inventory, sail dates, structural/moisture history and price flexibility. Main question is whether Max would enjoy the much leaner interior enough to justify the performance gain.
listed_date_notes: Earliest dated MLS image in listing 10043897 is Jan 8, 2026.
notes: PERFORMANCE BENCHMARK. Listing says steady 8–10 knots on passage is not unusual; much faster than Lagoon lane, but comfort compromise is substantial.

name: Seawind 1160 Lite – Vero Beach
why: Exceptionally young/light performance platform first commissioned in 2023 with only ~140h on twin 25hp Yamaha high-thrust outboards. 2025 upgrades include 1.25kW solar, 1,320Ah LiFePO4, 3kW inverter/charger, portable 2.8kW generator and bottom work. Three cabins and large 185-gallon water capacity; US imported with no tariffs.
risks: Only one head and much less interior/storage volume than the 42–46 ft boats. Outboard propulsion is simple/light but less conventional for long bluewater motoring. No permanent A/C or watermaker is disclosed, and standing-rig/sail condition still needs verification. Likely $20–40k to reach Max's comfort/off-grid target despite the young hull.
stage: New performance lead — not contacted; secondary outreach candidate
next_step: Secondary outreach: confirm watermaker/A-C absence, rig/sail dates, offshore history, exact lithium installation and realistic price. Compare against Plot Twist to determine whether young hull/low hours justify less liveaboard equipment.
listed_date_notes: Earliest dated MLS media for the same vessel is Oct 27, 2025; current URL uses a newer syndication ID.
notes: YOUNG PERFORMANCE OPTION. Very appealing age and systems, but smaller/leaner living arrangement means it needs to win decisively on sailing experience to beat larger boats.
